column2: req_desc

Four task lists
The board shows Habits, Dailies, To-dos and Rewards as four lists whose rows carry the published accessible names, and a player adds a task to each with the "New task" dialog.

Keyboard-complete board
Every board action works from the keyboard with the published keys, dialogs keep Tab inside them, and closing any dialog returns focus to the row that opened it.

Keyboard reorder
Alt+ArrowUp and Alt+ArrowDown move the focused task one place, keep focus on it, announce its new position and the order persists after reload.

Task API and ordering
The task endpoints create, read, edit, delete and move tasks with contiguous positions, and conflicting moves apply in arrival order.

Stale edit protection
An edit carrying an outdated updatedAt answers 409 stale_task, changes nothing and shows the published stale copy in the "Edit task" dialog.

Own lists live on every device
A change to a player's lists, totals or settings made on one device appears on that player's other open screens within 2 seconds without reload.

Reward formulas
Completing, checking and scoring pay experience, gold and boss damage by the published difficulty, value-band and rounding rules.

Task value and bands
Each task's value moves by the published steps within -20 to 20, and its row chip shows the band name for the current value.

Habit scoring journey
A player scores a habit up and down from the keyboard and sees the experience, gold, health, row score and band chip change and hears the feed sentence.

Checklist to-dos
A to-do's checklist items tick independently for no reward and raise the to-do's completion reward by the published checklist bonus.

Undo window
Unticking a daily or to-do inside the undo window reverts exactly what the tick gave, and after the window an untick changes no total, as qualified in Business rules.

Undo seen by the party
An undo inside the window restores the player's level, experience, health and gold and the boss health on the player's screen and every teammate's screen without reload.

Gold ledger
Every gold movement is a ledger entry of a published kind and the shown balance always equals the sum of the entries.

Refused purchases
Buying a reward priced above the balance answers 422 with the published gold error, shows it, and changes nothing.

Buying rewards from the keyboard
A player buys a reward with the keyboard, sees the gold fall by exactly its price, sees the refusal for an unaffordable one and keeps focus on the reward row.

Server-settled day close
The server closes each player's local date once at their day-start hour in their zone, running the published steps in order, and a repeated run changes nothing.

Daylight-saving closes
A day-start hour inside a spring-forward gap closes at the first instant after the gap and one inside a fall-back repeat closes at its first occurrence, once per date.

Zone and day-start settings
Settings validate the time zone and day-start hour, show the server's next day start, and a change takes effect from the next close without skipping or repeating a date.

Server-decided due state
Due-today, done state and the next day start come from the server and stay correct when the device clock is wrong.

Missed dailies journey
A player whose day closes with missed dailies sees the health loss, reset streaks and kept streaks on reload exactly as the close computed them.

Rest mode rules
A resting player's close costs no health, keeps streaks and adds no strike-back, they take no strike-back from others, and their strikes still count.

Resting journey
A player turns rest mode on with the switch, sees the rest banner, and after a close neither they nor their teammate lose health to their missed dailies.

Levels
Experience levels the player up at the published thresholds with carry-over and refills health on every level gained.

Fainting
Health reaching zero costs one level (never below 1), resets experience in the level, takes the published share of gold and resets health.

Level-up and faint dialogs
A level-up or faint, live or waiting from a close, opens its dialog with the published copy and closing it returns focus where it came from.

Level-up badge motion
The level-up badge grows to full size in about half a second and under reduced motion appears at full size at once.

Parties and invites
A leader forms a party and invites by username within the party-size limit, and invitees join or decline, as qualified in Business rules.

Quest lifecycle
A quest moves invited, active, then defeated or abandoned only along the published edges, with the published rejection for every other move.

Party chat
Members send chat messages of 1 to 500 characters within the chat rate limit, and the limit answers 429 with the published composer copy.

Live party journey
A leader and a member in two browsers see the invite, the acceptance, chat, the quest start and each strike arrive on the other screen without reload.

Live stream
One server-sent event stream delivers every published live change to every screen it concerns within 2 seconds.

Strikes in server order
Strikes from different members apply to the boss in the order the server receives them, and every member sees the same strike lines in that order.

Idempotent ticks
A tick, score or purchase repeated with one Idempotency-Key counts once and returns the stored response, and the same key with a different request answers 409.

Defeat and quest reward
The strike that takes the boss to 0.0 defeats the quest and pays every member the quest reward exactly once.

Simultaneous strikes journey
Two members tick at the same moment and both screens show both strikes, in the same order, with the boss meter matching the server.

Strike-back
During an active quest a close with missed dailies makes the boss strike back once, attributed to the player who missed, against every member who is not resting.

Strike-back seen live
When a teammate's close strikes back, every non-resting member's health meter and strike list update without reload and the feed announces the loss.

Game feed announcements
The polite "Game feed" region announces each published event in its exact sentence.

Phone board and party dialog
At 375 by 812 a player switches lists with the "Lists" tabs by tap or keyboard and opens the party rail as the "Party" dialog.

Swipe to complete
On a touch screen, a rightward swipe of at least 80 px on a daily or to-do row completes it and a shorter swipe does nothing.

Responsive layouts and touch targets
The board takes the published arrangement at 375, 768 and 1280 px wide with no horizontal overflow and every control at least 44 by 44 px on phone.

Task-list import format
An import file is checked against the published format and any error rejects the whole file with every error listed by line in the published wording.

Stored import originals
Every checked import file is stored byte for byte under its published key before any task is created, and "Download original" returns those bytes.

Upload type and size limits
Import files and banners of the wrong type or over their size limit are refused with 413 or 415 and the published copy before anything is stored.

Import journey
A player imports a file with errors, sees each error by line in the dialog, imports the fixed file, and finds both in import history with their results.

Storage outage
With the object store unreachable, import and banner upload answer 503 with the published copy and create nothing, while every other feature keeps working.

Party banner
A leader's banner is stored under its published key before success is reported, is served only to members, and replaces the old one live on every member's quest screen.

Quest history
Every finished quest is listed in each participant's quest history with each member's total damage and every strike and strike-back line, after reload and after leaving.

Party privacy
Another party's party, chat, quest, banner and history answer exactly like ones that do not exist, with 404.

Banner and history journey
A member sees the leader's new banner live, sees the quest fall, finds it in quest history after reload, and gets the not-found screen for another party's quest.

Local accounts
Players sign up and sign in with a username and password under the published rules and stay signed in by the session cookie.

Grading routes
The token-guarded setup and rollover routes create the published records in one transaction and run due closes exactly as the scheduler would.

One error order
Every endpoint applies the published error order and error body shapes.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from /app/run.json on port 4173 and answers the health check as published.

Server boundary
The server serves only the app and its API on one origin, enforces the published body limits, and never serves source files or credentials.

Health Seam
The boss panel's seam sits at the boss's remaining share of health, runs the published strike sequence, reaches the hot-pink defeat field once, and shows end states at once under reduced motion.

Duotone field look
Every screen is built from flat, square-cornered blush and aubergine fields that trade places at each section break, with hot pink used once per page.

Landing hero
The signed-out landing page shows the split hero with the cropped headline field on one side and the boss field on the other.

Landing demo quest
The landing page's three sample dailies strike a demo boss on the page without signing in, ending in the defeat field on the third tick.

Credentials from the environment
Every service credential and URL is read from the environment at start and never hard-coded or sent to the browser.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) with version and licence, plus the bundled Hubot Sans and Mona Sans fonts.
Every shipped package and bundled font is licensed MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or OFL-1.1.

The only datastores are the provided Postgres database and object store bucket: no SQLite, Redis, file-based or in-memory store of game state that outlives a request, apart from live stream connections.
The app loads no external network resources at runtime: no CDN scripts, styles or web fonts.
A package-lock.json is committed and install uses it.
The provided service configuration (dev compose files and their seeded credentials) is left unchanged.
